body: Board event + operational fix entry. (1) PR #95 (GTimG/QuasiRiemannTracker, author josephbebel - new contributor, created 2026-10-29T12:59:28Z, head branch joint-detector-source-curves-8738357029730854, submission submissions/2026-10-29-joint-detector-source-curves/): claims Dirichlet nonvanishing for every positive modulus and every character when Re(s) > 4369178514865427/5000000000000000 = 0.8738357029730854 (only excluding the principal pole; 'no analytic or source-provider premise'). If merged below the anchor, the in-tree face would shrink from d0max = 0.37387234 to 0.3738357029730854 (a 3.6637027e-5 step - about half the 0211 step, the 8th supersession). Method per the PR body: selected ordinary-source sextic norm + fixed positive amplitude gap, repeated-mark counting, feedback from global Hecke bounds, finite source transfer along strictly certified polynomial curves; a 459-piece curve with explicit cap extension for a complete 284-window return; 4,260 admission guards, 1,826 HIGH regions. Direct source dependencies: OpenAI, Hailey Collet, ArviFoxy, Sil, Jacob Sussman (the existing lineage + Sussman). Self-declared: Candidate.bound compiled locally on Lean 4.34.1 with axiom closure {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}; 'the isolated rebuild of this exported source package is still in progress' - i.e. a self-UNVERIFIED build claim, which is exactly what the section-8 conveyor re-proves from the pinned commit. Protocol discipline (unchanged since 0131): UNMERGED = claimed, not board-best; B6 fires ONLY on a merged official-catalogue record below 43693617/50000000 (watcher exit 10) -> then run scripts/rh/b6/b6_preflight.py (detect -> pinned-commit fetch -> statement boundary identity -> build-cone byte-identity vs frozen copies -> stage C per-module kernel compile -> stage D canonical compile/axiom audit/zeta probe/0-sorry sweep -> ADOPTABLE verdict) -> in-tree module + RHEnd B22 + gates + docs. (2) The operational defect found and fixed while confirming this: tracker_watch2.py's pending-detail print line formatted the open-PR pending row's bound with '{b:.9f}' where b is None by construction (the open-PR row carries no single numeric bound) -> TypeError rc=1, and because the print preceded alert(2, ...), the level-2 alert + B6-PENDING-* marker writes were silently skipped for the cycles in which the crash happened. Timeline (watcher_0212.log, 117 cycles 09:40:52Z-19:17:48Z): 41 rc=0 (quiet) cycles; PR #95 opened 12:59:28Z falls between the 12:57:26Z (rc=0) and 13:02:26Z (rc=1) cycles; error window = exactly 3 rc=1 cycles (13:02:26, 13:07:27, 13:12:28Z); the patched script (n/a-safe format + try/except around the detail print + alert write kept intact) was deployed via a daemon restart, after which 73 consecutive correct rc=11 cycles wrote a B6-PENDING-* marker + level-2 WATCHER_ALERT.json every 5 minutes through 19:17:48Z. A later session-cleanup killed that daemon process (detached-via-foreground child of an aborted command); it was re-deployed at 19:22:34Z fully detached (setsid nohup, session leader, survives turn cleanup): pid 2139718, first cycle rc=11 correct, pidfile + log + markers all consistent. (3) State: the in-tree face is UNCHANGED ([Z78ArviDensity] 0.87387234 remains the terminal face; the 41-record catalogue is the gate and has no merged record below it). No RH claim. The B6 review packet now carries the eighth pending (PR #95) alongside the seven demonstrated runs (0131/0133, 0142, 0162, 0195, 0200, 0203, 0211); on merge, this same entry's audit packet (tmp/b6audit/tracker/pr95_pending_audit.json: meta + body + exact rational) is the starting point for the conveyor run.
